title: How the hunt for human retroviruses led to the discovery of interleukin-2 and a path to immunotherapy.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Ran scripts/paper_context.py (no PMCID, isOpenAccess=N, hasSuppl=N, hasData=N, hasDbCrossReferences=N, hasTMAccessionNumbers=N; zero accessions, zero NCBI links, zero Zenodo/Dryad hits). Cross-checked Crossref and the Europe PMC core record: type 'journal-article', PubMed publication types 'Historical Article' + 'Journal Article', volume 393, issue 6816, pages 1078-1079 (two pages), 15 references, authors Rafi Ahmed (Emory) and Steven Rosenberg (NCI). There are no data files to open because the article has none.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Only the one-sentence abstract was retrievable: 'Fifty years ago, research into human retroviruses yielded unexpected findings.' No full text, no methods, no data availability statement exists for this item.

a1_downloadable.note: No dataset of any kind. This is a two-page retrospective commentary marking 50 years since interleukin-2 (IL-2, an immune signalling protein) was discovered; it reports no new measurements, has no supplementary files, no repository accessions and no data availability statement. Verified against Crossref and the Europe PMC core record, not just the abstract.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: There is no table, so there is no column and no label. Any prediction target would have to be built from scratch out of other people's datasets, which is the exact A2 failure mode.

a3_inputs_present.note: No sequences, structures, compounds or measurements accompany the article.

a4_units_stated.note: No measured values at all, therefore no units.

a5_enough_rows.note: Zero rows. The article is narrative prose across two printed pages with 15 references.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially fits, because there is nothing to load. Passing here is meaningless given A1.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: No counts are claimed and none can be checked.

a8_label_provenance.note: No label exists, so its provenance cannot be traced to a physical measurement.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: the article contains no data, so no model could be trained or evaluated from it.

plain_idea.one_liner: No usable project; the nearest idea considered was predicting which patients respond to interleukin-2 immunotherapy from their tumour data.
plain_idea.train_on: Nothing is provided by this article. The idea considered would need an external cohort of melanoma or kidney-cancer patients treated with high-dose interleukin-2 (IL-2, an immune-stimulating protein) with tumour molecular profiles attached; this paper supplies zero such examples.
plain_idea.predict: Response to interleukin-2 therapy, where the true answer would come from clinical tumour-shrinkage assessments in a treatment trial. None of those records are in or linked to this article.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: The underlying clinical question matters to oncologists deciding who should receive a toxic therapy, but this particular article contributes only historical narrative and cannot support it.

ml_idea: None available from this article. Any interleukin-2 immunotherapy-response model would have to be built entirely from unrelated external resources (for example clinical trial cohorts or The Cancer Genome Atlas), with this article contributing nothing but background reading.

effort.compute_note: No compute estimate is meaningful because there is no dataset; nothing was timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Look at the Europe PMC publication-type field and the page range: 'Historical Article', pages 1078-1079, hasData=N. That is a ten-second check and it kills the candidate.

verdict_reason: Two-page historical Perspective in Science by Ahmed and Rosenberg on the 50th anniversary of interleukin-2's discovery. It is commentary, not research: no data files, no supplement, no accessions, no repository deposits, and it is behind a paywall with no full text in Europe PMC. Part A1 through A5 and A7 through A8 all fail for the same reason, so scoring stopped there. This paper should never have entered the candidate queue; a publication-type filter excluding 'Historical Article', 'Editorial', 'Comment' and 'News' would have caught it upstream.
